artworks.title: Bingham-Melcomb, Dorsetshire
artworks.medium: hand-colored lithograph on wove paper mounted to board
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Mrs. Benjamin Ogle Tayloe, 1879)
artworks.description: The image shows a stone building with ornate architectural details, climbing greenery on the walls, a group of people in period attire on a lawn with pink flowers, and a woman in a doorway. The sky has soft clouds. The color palette includes warm beiges and browns of the building, soft greens of the foliage, and occasional brighter hues of clothing and flowers.

artworks.title: Men at a Table
artworks.medium: pen and black ink on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: The image shows a line drawing of six individuals seated around a table. One person is seated on the left side facing forward, while the other five individuals are seated on the right side. Clothing details are minimal, and two rectangular objects are on the table. The background is plain. The drawing is signed "Logasa" with the date "8/3/32" beneath it.

artworks.title: Four Men
artworks.medium: pen and blue ink on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: The image is a line drawing of four men's faces, depicted from the shoulders up. The figures are positioned side by side, facing forward with varying head tilts and expressions. The first person has round glasses and a slightly balding head, with a serious expression. The second person has a youthful appearance with a smooth face and neatly combed hair. The third person has more pronounced facial features with a mustache and fuller head of hair. The fourth person wears a hat, with minimal facial details provided in the sketch. The drawing consists of thin lines on a plain background. The artist's signature "C Logasa" and the date "4/20/32" are at the bottom right corner of the image.

artworks.title: Hola, hé! Madame l'hotesse
artworks.medium: lithograph
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image depicts the upper body of a seated man in profile. He is facing to the right, with his left hand raised and pinching a thin line or thread in front of his face. He has a dark, slicked-back hair with curls on the sides and sideburns. The man is dressed in a dark jacket over a light collared shirt and a patterned cravat. On the table in front of him are a bottle, a filled glass, and a plate with a spoon. In the background, there is a printed page with text and the title "SILHOUETTES" at the top.

artworks.title: Le lecture du journal
artworks.medium: lithograph
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image is a monochrome illustration of an elderly man sitting in a semi-reclined position on a cushioned chair. The man's face is turned slightly to his right as he looks down, with exaggerated facial features. He has thinning, light-colored hair covered by a patterned hat. The man wears a dark jacket over a white shirt and is holding a paper in one hand while the other hand grips the side of the paper. In the background, there is a round table with a saucer and cup. Text in the background suggests that this illustration is part of a publication focused on visual and satirical content, with the header "SILHOUETTES" visible. The text below indicates he is reading a newspaper, with details in French.

artworks.title: Speke Hall, Lancashire
artworks.medium: hand-colored lithograph on wove paper mounted to board
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Mrs. Benjamin Ogle Tayloe, 1879)
artworks.description: This is a painting of Speke Hall in Lancashire. The artwork showcases the Tudor-style manor house with an archway entrance, half-timbered facade, finial-adorned roofline, large window above the arch, wooden beams, masonry, stone pathway, plants, stone features, and a sky with soft clouds. The style resembles Victorian-era architectural illustrations.

artworks.title: Hudson River
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Membership Association Fund, 1949)
artworks.description: The image shows a view from a slightly elevated position across a river towards a distant waterfall and surrounding landscape. The horizon is high, meeting the tree line across the upper third of the image. The waterfall cascades over a rocky ledge, with structures nearby. The artwork uses a light and delicate brushstroke technique, depicting details with fine lines typical of pencil or graphite sketches. The color palette is monochrome, utilizing shades of grey to represent the natural elements. Close to us is a patch of land with low shrubbery and vegetation. In the background, there are dense forests providing a textured contrast to the water surface.

artworks.title: Head of a Boy
artworks.medium: charcoal on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, 1930)
artworks.description: The image is a drawing of a young person in profile view. The person is facing to the right, with their face in a side profile view, showing the head and part of the upper chest. The person has well-defined facial features with a gentle expression, smooth complexion, and soft characteristics. They have short tousled hair, likely drawn with charcoal. The individual is wearing a collared shirt and there are no visible objects or jewelry. The background is a plain, shaded surface, keeping the focus on the subject's profile.

artworks.title: La pipe matinale
artworks.medium: lithograph
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image features a profile view of a person reclining on a surface with their head on a pillow or similar support. The person is smoking a pipe, with smoke emanating from it. The individual has facial features including a pronounced nose and chin, with visible lines suggesting age or expression. They wear a cap or headscarf covering their head, leaving the face visible, and are dressed in loose-fitting nightwear or a robe. The setting appears to be informal and relaxed. French text, "La Pipe Matinale" (The Morning Pipe), is visible, as well as the words "SILHOUETTES." and "N°6" at the top. The background is shaded and textured, contrasting with the detailed drawing of the person, and the focus is on the individual.

artworks.title: Two Heads
artworks.medium: gouache and graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, 1968)
artworks.description: This abstract image contains a combination of angular and curved lines intersecting on the canvas. There are shapes resembling facial features and a figure that resembles a person or animal. The fragmented forms in shades of gray, black, green, and pink are surrounded by a blue frame, creating a complex composition.

artworks.title: Man Running from Elephants
artworks.medium: watercolor, gouache, and pen and black ink over graphite on wove paper mounted to board
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Bequest of James Parmelee, 1941)
artworks.description: This is a painting of a figure running away from a herd of elephants. The art style is reminiscent of Peter Newell. The image shows a figure in period attire sprinting across a landscape with detailed underbrush, accompanied by a stampede of elephants. The setting is under a bright sky, with the elephants appearing to be moving forward urgently. The painting captures motion, emotion, and humor through its portrayal of the scene.

artworks.title: A Neopolitan Beggar
artworks.medium: watercolor over graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mrs. Armistead Peter III [Caroline Ogden-Jones Peter], 1976)
artworks.description: The image shows an artistic depiction of a woman standing, angled slightly to her right. She has a defined profile and dark hair partially covered by a white headscarf. She wears traditional attire with earthy tones and decorative patterns, holding a small object in her left hand. The background is minimal and blurred, emphasizing the subject.

artworks.title: Terme di Caracalla, Roma
artworks.medium: watercolor over graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mrs. Armistead Peter III [Caroline Ogden-Jones Peter], 1976)
artworks.description: A small bouquet of flowers is shown in the center of the image. The flowers include large red poppies, purple, yellow, and light pink blooms, green leaves and stems. The color palette of the image consists of reds, greens, purples, and yellows against a light background. In the bottom left corner, the text "Terme di Caracalla, Roma - July 4, 92" is inscribed diagonally. The bouquet is centrally placed, with the poppies at the top and right, and smaller flowers scattered around.

artworks.title: Seacoast by Moonlight [recto]
artworks.medium: graphite with white crayon on gray paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of J. William Middendorf, II, 1977)
artworks.description: The image shows a sketchy seascape with a slightly elevated viewpoint. The horizon line is below the middle of the image, highlighting the sky and sea. Sailboats are visible on the horizon with choppy water and a cloudy sky. The brushstrokes are loose with a rough texture, suggesting movement in the water and clouds. The color palette is limited to shades of grey and white, creating a monochromatic effect. A rocky coastline is depicted in the distance on the right, while the water ripples energetically in the foreground.

artworks.title: The Hall, Speke, Lancashire
artworks.medium: hand-colored lithograph on wove paper mounted to board
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Mrs. Benjamin Ogle Tayloe, 1879)
artworks.description: This is a painting of an ornate hall interior with elaborate wood paneling and carvings on the walls. The ceiling features a geometric grid of coffered panels. Stained-glass windows allow light into the room, and the floor has black and white checkered tiles. A large table is surrounded by objects indicating a formal setting. Animal trophies and armor displays are on the walls. The painting is in the style of architectural renderings from the Victorian era.

artworks.title: A Quiet Nook
artworks.medium: etching in black on silk mounted to board
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Bequest of Frank B. Bristow, 1968)

artworks.title: Norwich, Connecticut
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Membership Association Fund, 1953)
artworks.description: The image is a pencil sketch of a waterside scene. There is a distant hill on the horizon. To the left, there is a structure resembling a dock or shipyard with a mast. The drawing has delicate lines and shading. The color palette is monochromatic with varying shades of gray on ivory paper. On the hill, there are outlines of trees and a building, possibly a house or chapel. Furthermore, there are sails of other boats visible. The water reflects the masts and lines, showing a subtle ripple effect.

artworks.title: York River
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Membership Association Fund, 1953)
artworks.description: The image features a sketched river landscape from an elevated vantage point. A line of trees, small buildings, and a bridge are visible in the distance. The sketch is defined by light pencil strokes on a cream paper background in various shades of gray. Closest to us on the right, small boats are tethered to a wooden dock. Trees flank the riverbank on the left, extending into the distance.

artworks.title: Newburyport
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Membership Association Fund, 1953)
artworks.description: The image shows a pencil sketch of a rural landscape viewed from a slightly elevated point, capturing a village scene in the distance. The horizon is set in the upper third of the composition with small buildings and chimneys emitting smoke. The sketch features light pencil strokes creating texture for the trees and buildings. The transition from the closer trees to the village beyond is smooth. The color palette is monochromatic with pencil on paper creating contrast. The sky above the horizon is left blank, directing focus to the detailed line work capturing the essence of the village.

artworks.title: St. Paul's from Under Waterloo Bridge, Low Tide
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Membership Association Fund, 1949)
artworks.description: The image displays a riverside cityscape seen from a low vantage point near the water. The city has various structures, including a large domed building that could be a cathedral. Sailing vessels with tall masts are on the right side of the image. The city structures are drawn with fine pencil lines, and the overall color scheme is monochrome. The water reflects part of the cityscape, and the sky is left blank, drawing attention to the detailed architecture.

artworks.title: L'habitué de la boutique de Félix
artworks.medium: lithograph
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image shows a man standing from the waist up, with a tilted head and gaze towards the viewer. He has distinct facial features, including a noticeable nose and chin, along with pronounced eyebrows. The man has a receding hairline and light, possibly grayish hair. He is dressed in a dark coat or sweater over a white shirt. Beside him is a table with pastries on a tiered stand. The man is holding a small pastry in his raised left hand. The background is lightly shaded with text and faint patterns, suggesting it may be part of a book or publication.

artworks.title: The Pescatory
artworks.medium: graphite and red colored pencil on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, 1960)
artworks.description: This pencil drawing shows a perspective close to a body of water, looking at a stone bridge structure. The scene focuses on the immediate landscape with emphasis on the bridge. Two arched openings are visible under the bridge, with a small building on top and a figure to its side. The brushwork is light, creating a soft texture. The color palette is monochromatic in shades of gray. Tall trees surround the bridge, with water reflecting the elements faintly.

artworks.title: Annie
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Robert McIntyre, 1947)
artworks.description: The image is a pencil drawing of a person's side profile. The person is sitting, leaning forward with their face on crossed arms on the back of a chair. They have neatly styled hair, closed eyes, and are wearing a long-sleeved garment. The fingers are gripping the chair. The background has minimal details like a shape and writing with the artist's initials and the date.

artworks.title: Boy Reading
artworks.medium: pen and brown ink on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Robert McIntyre, 1947)
artworks.description: The illustration depicts an upper body profile of a person who is seated and reading a book. The individual is wearing a hat with a small brim and a band, and is dressed in a long-sleeved garment. They are shown against a background with foliage and some crosshatching for shading. A handwritten note is included under the illustration.
